Priya (AE): Intro: We're onboarding a large fintech POC. They require Private deployment in ap-southeast-1 + eu-central-1. Security constraints: strict /32 allowlist only, no transit gateways, no cross-region peering. They asked: can Redwood provide per-region static egress IPs (single /32 each)? Also need sample firewall snippet and any hidden pricing for static IPs or SLA tradeoffs.
Marco (NetEng): Short answer: yes, we can provide per-region static egress IPs as single /32s, but only under a reserved capacity / dedicated egress agreement. Without that, we advertise ranges (AWS/Azure) which are too large.
Priya (AE): Customer insists on us owning the IPs rather than using their NAT. They want us to be the source IP for outbound traffic so downstream partners allowlist us. Feasible?
Rina (Solutions): Feasible if they accept the enterprise add-on: we provision a dedicated egress pool per region that terminates from our connectors. Ops notes: - We'll deploy connectors in each requested region behind a fixed EIP per connector. - If they want a single IP for both regions, not possible without routing traffic across region (which they disallowed).
Omar (Security): Security note: We'll need to run an IP ownership and abuse check with our cloud provider and legal — this takes ~7 business days. Also requires their contract to include the reserved-eips clause and indemnity for IP abuse.
Priya (AE): Can we give them a minimal firewall snippet for their compliance team?
Marco (NetEng): Paste below — replace PLACEHOLDER_IP with the assigned /32s.
```
# Firewall egress allowlist - example
# Allow HTTPS to Redwood connectors (replace with assigned IPs)
ALLOW TCP 443 to PLACEHOLDER_IP_AP_SOUTHEAST_1/32  # ap-southeast-1 connector egress
ALLOW TCP 443 to PLACEHOLDER_IP_EU_CENTRAL_1/32  # eu-central-1 connector egress
# Health probes from our monitoring (optional)
ALLOW TCP 443 to 198.51.100.12/32  # monitoring probe
# Optional outbound DNS to route53 health checks
ALLOW UDP 53 to 169.254.169.253/32  # sample internal resolver (if applicable)
```
Priya (AE): Good. What about TLS termination — can we keep end-to-end TLS to customer's backend?
Rina (Solutions): Yes. In Private deployments we support end-to-end TLS. Options: - Customer-managed certs on their connectors (recommended) - Redwood-managed certs (requires certificate delegation and is less common for fintech)
Omar (Security): Add to questionnaire answers: - Key custody: we support customer-managed KMS integration for Private deployments. - Audit logs: available via secure S3 bucket export; default retention 90 days. - Pen test: we provide infrastructure diagrams and will coordinate scoping under NDA.
Priya (AE): Great. Pricing ask: how to brief them on monthly delta for reserved egress / per-region dedicated IP?
Rina (Solutions): Rough pricing bullets you can use: - Base Private deployment license (per-region) — includes connectors and standard telemetry. - Reserved egress IPs: per-IP monthly surcharge + one-time provisioning fee. Typical ballpark: $X00/month per /32 plus one-time $Y00 provisioning (tailor per deal). - SLA: connectors standard 99.9% per-region; recommend 2 connectors/region for higher availability.
Marco (NetEng): Also mention lead times: IP provisioning + legal review ~1-2 weeks, reserved capacity provisioning and engineering validation ~2-4 weeks depending on complexity.
Priya (AE): Customer also asked if we can do cross-region DNS failover while keeping traffic regional (they want geo-failover but no cross-region egress). Thoughts?
Marco (NetEng): Pattern: deploy local connectors in each region, create region-specific hostnames and use DNS failover (health checks). If a region fails, failover will direct clients to another region but that will be cross-region egress — so only use if customer allows that during failover. If they categorically ban cross-region egress, then failover must be manual or at application level, not DNS.
Omar (Security): For compliance: document failover behavior clearly in the runbook. If cross-region egress is possible during failover, they must update supplier risk assessment.
infra-bot: Ticket created: SD-7201 Reserved EIP request + SOC questionnaire task.
Rina (Solutions): Next steps: @Priya collect which regions require reserved IPs and whether cross-region failover is permitted. @Marco will produce an itemized cost estimate for reserved IPs. @Omar will draft the short answers to their security questionnaire for the IP ownership and TLS/KMS items.
Priya (AE): I'll send this to the customer now and ask them to confirm: 1) list of regions that must have /32s; 2) allowlist for temporary cross-region failover? Also asking if they will accept FQDN allowlisting instead of IPs.
Marco (NetEng): One more technical footnote: if customer's network uses strict source validation, we may need to support proxy protocol or preserve original client IPs — that requires additional connector config and may be limited. I'll call out in the quote.
Priya (AE): Thanks all. I'll update ticket SD-7201 when I hear back.
